title: Natural semilinear inverse-image module stalk comparison
statement: For ringed spaces X,Y, continuous f:X→Y and x in X, let k:OY_(f x)→(inverseImageRing f OY)_x be stalkPullbackHom followed by stalk of toSheafify. There exist additive equivalences c_M:M_(f x)≃(inverseImageModule f OY M)_x, simultaneously semilinear c_M(r m)=k(r)c_M(m) and natural c_N(a_(f x)(m))=(inverseImageModuleMap a)_x(c_M(m)). Inverse-image module structures are those of [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module], source module stalks those of [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], and additive stalk maps those of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. There is no scalar extension, alpha, or beta in this statement.

proof.text: Use the explicit inverse-image construction, whose underlying presheaf is presheaf pullback followed by sheafification. Define the comparison map as stalkPullbackHom followed by stalkFunctor.map toSheafify, for both the ring and each abelian sheaf. Mathlib stalkPullbackIso and stalkFunctor_map_unit_toSheafify_isIso make the abelian comparison invertible; convert asIso to an additive equivalence. No abstract chosen left adjoint or uniqueness-of-adjoints comparison is needed.

Prove the germ formula for the explicit map using germ_stalkPullbackHom and stalkFunctor_map_germ. Unfold sheafAdjunctionContinuous and use map_restrictFullyFaithful_unit_app and comp_unit_app to identify the section map with the explicit sheaf adjunction unit. These are categorical adjunction identities applied to the construction, with no additional geometric theorem.

Represent the scalar and vector by germs, then restrict their representatives to the intersection of the two neighborhoods. Use germ_smul in the source. The chosen-spec semilinearity clause of exists_inverseImageModuleInstances transports the product under the explicit sheaf unit. Use germ_smul in the inverse-image module and the ring and abelian comparison germ formulas to identify this with k(r) times c(m).

Represent a source module stalk element by a germ. Unfold moduleStalkFunctor.map and stalkAddMap, then apply stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply on both sides. The abelian comparison germ formula reduces the desired equation to sectionwise unit_naturality of the explicit sheaf pullback adjunction. inverseImageModuleMap has precisely that underlying abelian pullback map, by definition.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_inverseImage_stalk_comparison_natural
    (X Y : RingedSpace.{u}) (f : X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier) (x : X) :
    let k : Y.presheaf.stalk (f x) ⟶
        TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X.carrier)
          (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f Y.sheaf).obj x :=
      TopCat.Presheaf.stalkPullbackHom CommRingCat.{u} f Y.presheaf x ≫
      (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat.{u} x).map
        (toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          ((TopCat.Presheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f).obj Y.presheaf))
    ∃ (c : ∀ M : RingedSpace.Modules Y,
      (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y (f x)).obj M ≃+
        TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X.carrier)
          (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModule f Y.sheaf M).val.presheaf x),
      (∀ (M : RingedSpace.Modules Y) (r : Y.presheaf.stalk (f x))
        (m : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y (f x)).obj M),
        c M (r • m) = k.hom r • c M m) ∧
      ∀ (M N : RingedSpace.Modules Y) (a : M ⟶ N)
      (m : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y (f x)).obj M),
      c N ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y (f x)).map a m) =
      PresheafOfModules.stalkAddMap
          (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModuleMap f Y.sheaf M a).val (c M m)
